text:
Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When your code doesn't work, the first step is identifying the bug. Instead of guessing randomly, use a systematic approach. Start by narrowing down where the problem occurs, checking recent changes, and testing small parts of the code.

Modern debugging tools make this much easier. A debugger allows you to pause the program at any line and inspect variables in real time. This helps you see exactly what the computer is doing. Additionally, logging is a simple but powerful technique. By printing messages or values to the console at key points, you can trace the flow of your program and spot where logic goes wrong.

Remember, patience and a clear plan are your best friends when fixing errors.
